falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Recruit a multi-subject dataset (≥30 subjects) spanning diverse autonomic phenotypes (athletes, heart failure patients, healthy controls) with gold-standard autonomic assessments (24h HRV RMSSD, baroreflex sensitivity, LF/HF ratio). Apply conformal prediction with a subject-agnostic calibration set. Stratify subjects by autonomic phenotype tertiles and compute conditional coverage per subject. Fit a linear mixed model: |coverage_deviation| ~ phenotype_tertile + (1|subject) + age + medication_class + fitness. Test the fixed effect of tertile (ANOVA, α=0.05). Compute partial Spearman correlation between inter-subject CV of RMSSD and coverage deviation controlling for age, medication, fitness. If the tertile effect is non-significant (p>0.05) and partial ρ < 0.2 (p>0.05), the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: No significant effect of autonomic phenotype tertile on absolute coverage deviation (p > 0.05) and partial Spearman correlation between inter-subject RMSSD CV and coverage deviation < 0.2 (p > 0.05) after controlling for age, medication, and fitness.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Multi-subject physiological dataset with ≥30 subjects covering diverse autonomic phenotypes; gold-standard autonomic assessments per subject (24h HRV RMSSD, baroreflex sensitivity, LF/HF ratio); standardized segment labels (supine rest, paced breathing, orthostatic challenge) with ≥50 segments per subject; conformal prediction pipeline with subject-agnostic calibration set.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Residual confounding by unmeasured factors (e.g., undiagnosed conditions, genetic factors) that correlate with both autonomic phenotype and coverage deviation, creating a spurious association.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient statistical power due to small sample size per tertile (<10) or high within-subject variability masking the effect; or the conformal method used inadvertently adapts to subject-level heterogeneity (e.g., via feature normalization), reducing coverage deviations.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Collect wearable sensor data with synchronized triaxial accelerometer and ECG/PPG (≥100 hours) and ground-truth activity labels (video-annotated: sitting, walking, running). Segment data into fixed-length windows (30s) aligned to activity bouts. Compute segment-level artifact metrics: accelerometer variance (g²), ECG baseline wander amplitude (mV), SNR (dB). Apply conformal prediction using motion-sensitive features (HRV time-domain, morphological features). Fit a beta regression: coverage ~ activity_label + segment_duration + placement_score + impedance. Test the activity_label effect (Wald test, α=0.05). Compute Spearman correlations between artifact metrics and coverage error per segment. If activity_label effect is non-significant (p>0.05) and correlations are non-significant (|ρ|<0.2, p>0.05) after controlling for confounders, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Conditional coverage difference between high-motion (walking/running) and resting (sitting) segments < 5 percentage points after controlling for segment duration, sensor placement, and skin impedance, and correlation between accelerometer variance and coverage error not significant (p > 0.05).
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Wearable dataset with synchronized triaxial accelerometer and ECG/PPG (≥100 hours); ground-truth activity labels (video-annotated or protocol-defined) for segments: sitting, walking, running; segment-level artifact metrics: accelerometer variance (g²), ECG baseline wander amplitude (mV), SNR (dB); conformal prediction features sensitive to motion (HRV time-domain, morphological features).
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Uncontrolled sensor displacement during activity that changes electrode contact independently of motion artifacts, creating a spurious activity-coverage association.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient motion intensity range in the dataset (e.g., only slow walking) to induce substantial artifact-related distribution shift; or the conformal features used are inherently robust to motion artifacts (e.g., frequency-domain HRV), masking the effect.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Obtain a polysomnography dataset (≥50 subjects) with full sleep staging (N1,N2,N3,REM,Wake) and continuous ECG, respiration, EDA. Define coarse segment labels (sleep vs. wake). Identify transition segments (stage change within window) and stable segments (no stage change). Compute conditional coverage per latent sleep stage within the same coarse label. Perform a paired t-test (or Wilcoxon) comparing coverage in transition vs. stable segments matched on coarse label. Estimate mutual information between latent state and nonconformity scores (kNN estimator) and test significance via permutation (α=0.05). Control for circadian phase, temperature, apnea severity via stratified analysis. If no significant coverage difference (p>0.05, mean difference <3%) and mutual information not significantly >0, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between transition and stable segments within the same coarse label after controlling for circadian phase, temperature, and apnea (paired t-test p > 0.05, mean difference < 3%), and mutual information between latent state and nonconformity scores not significantly greater than zero (permutation p > 0.05).
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Polysomnography dataset with ≥50 subjects, full sleep staging (N1,N2,N3,REM,Wake); continuous ECG, respiration, EDA with coarse segment labels (sleep/wake); gold-standard latent state annotations: sleep stage transitions; conformal prediction using only coarse labels as covariates.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Circadian phase or temperature changes coincident with stage transitions that independently affect signal distribution, creating a spurious transition-coverage link.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient temporal resolution to capture brief autonomic transitions (e.g., micro-arousals) or the conformal nonconformity score is insensitive to the specific physiological changes during transitions (e.g., using only HRV features that change slowly).

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Acquire long-term monitoring data (>48h) with precise timestamps (≥30 subjects) and circadian phase markers (core body temperature, melatonin, cortisol). Stratify segments into 4-hour circadian phase bins. Apply conformal prediction without time-of-day covariates, controlling for sleep/wake state. Fit a cosinor model: coverage ~ mesor + amplitude*cos(2π*time/24 + phase). Test amplitude ≠ 0 (F-test, α=0.05). Correlate coverage deviation amplitude with HRV_RMSSD diurnal amplitude across subjects. If available, analyze a constant routine subset (controlled posture, dim light, hourly isocaloric snacks) to test coverage stability under controlled conditions. If cosinor amplitude is non-significant (p>0.05) or <2%, and no correlation with HRV diurnal amplitude after controlling for activity, meals, light, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Cosinor model fit not significant (p > 0.05 for amplitude), or coverage amplitude < 2%, or no correlation between HRV diurnal amplitude and coverage deviation amplitude after controlling for activity, meals, light (partial Pearson r < 0.2, p > 0.05).
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Long-term monitoring dataset >48h with precise timestamps (≥30 subjects); circadian phase markers: core body temperature, melatonin, cortisol (or validated proxies); segments stratified into 4-hour circadian phase bins; conformal prediction without time-of-day covariates, with sleep/wake control.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Behavioral patterns (e.g., morning exercise, meal timing) that correlate with circadian phase and independently cause distribution shifts, masquerading as endogenous rhythm effects.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient monitoring duration (<48h) to resolve circadian rhythm; or the conformal calibration set inadvertently includes a representative sample of all circadian phases, masking the effect.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Use a dataset with quantified annotation quality: multiple expert annotations per segment, or algorithmic pre-labels with confidence, or a gold-truth subset (≥500 segments). Estimate annotation error rate per segment type via inter-rater agreement or vs. gold truth. Compute conditional coverage per segment type. Fit a linear model: coverage_deviation ~ error_rate + SQI + fatigue_index + prelabel_confidence. Test the error_rate coefficient (t-test, α=0.05). Compute asymmetry index (under_coverage_rate - over_coverage_rate) per segment type. Perform KS test for nonconformity score distribution shift between clean and noisy labels. If error_rate coefficient is non-significant (p>0.05) after matching on SQI and controlling for fatigue, and asymmetry index not significantly different from zero, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: No significant correlation between annotation error rate and coverage deviation after matching on SQI and controlling for fatigue (partial ρ < 0.2, p > 0.05), and asymmetry index not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Dataset with quantified annotation quality: multiple expert annotations per segment, or algorithmic pre-labels with confidence, or gold-truth subset (≥500 segments); segment difficulty scores; annotation metadata: expert fatigue (session duration), pre-label confidence; conformal prediction using noisy labels as ground truth.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Segment difficulty correlating with both annotation error and signal quality (low SNR), causing a spurious error-coverage correlation that is actually driven by SNR.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Annotation errors that are symmetric (equal false positive and false negative rates) canceling out coverage effects; or the gold-truth subset is too small to reliably estimate error rates per segment type.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Start with a calibration set with known segment proportions reflecting operational prevalence (e.g., arrhythmia types: AFib 1%, VT 0.1%, normal 98.9%). Sub-sample the calibration set to create 10 prevalence ratios. For each, compute conditional coverage per segment. Fit a linear model on log-log scale: log(|deviation|) ~ log(n_segment). Test if slope = -0.5 (t-test, α=0.05). Compare rare vs. common segments matched on signal variability and subject representation (paired test). If the log-log slope is not significantly different from 0 (p>0.05) and matched rare segments show deviations <5% when sub-sampled to same n_segment, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Log-log slope of deviation vs. n_segment not significantly different from 0 (p > 0.05), or rare segments with matched variability/subject representation show deviations <5% when sub-sampled to same n_segment.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Calibration set with known segment proportions reflecting operational prevalence (e.g., arrhythmia types: AFib 1%, VT 0.1%, normal 98.9%); sufficient test samples per segment (≥200) to estimate conditional coverage reliably; conformal prediction with marginal coverage guarantee only; ability to sub-sample calibration set to vary segment_prevalence_ratio.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Rare segments having inherently higher signal variability or coming from different subjects/sessions, causing coverage deviations that are attributed to sample size but actually due to heterogeneity.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: The conformal method used (e.g., with regularization) is robust to small calibration sample sizes, or the test set is too small to reliably estimate conditional coverage for rare segments, masking the deviation.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Collect physiological time series with characterized autocorrelation: ECG (HRV), EEG, BPV (≥20 subjects, ≥1h each). Estimate autocorrelation time constant τ per signal per subject. Create non-overlapping, stationarity-verified segments (KPSS test) of fixed length (30s, 60s, 300s) with varying spacing (0, τ, 5τ, 10τ). Apply standard conformal prediction ignoring temporal dependence and block conformal as benchmark. Fit a mixed model: coverage ~ spacing/τ + lag1_autocorr + stationarity_pvalue + (1|subject). Test the spacing/τ coefficient. If coverage does not decrease with lag-1 autocorrelation after controlling for non-stationarity and overlap (partial ρ > -0.2, p>0.05) and coverage is nominal even at zero spacing when segments are stationary and non-overlapping, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: No significant correlation between autocorrelation strength and coverage deviation after controlling for non-stationarity and overlap (partial ρ > -0.2, p > 0.05), or coverage nominal even at zero spacing when segments are stationary and non-overlapping.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Physiological time series with characterized autocorrelation: ECG (HRV), EEG, BPV (≥20 subjects, ≥1h each); segments of fixed length (30s, 60s, 300s) with varying spacing (0s to 300s); standard conformal prediction ignoring temporal dependence; block conformal or dependent conformal method as benchmark.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Non-stationary mean/variance trends within segments (e.g., HRV drift) that correlate with autocorrelation and cause coverage drops, mistakenly attributed to autocorrelation.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Segment length too long relative to autocorrelation time constant, making effective sample size large enough that exchangeability violation is negligible; or the nonconformity score is based on features that are insensitive to temporal dependence (e.g., spectral features averaged over segment).

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Generate segments with controlled SNR variation by adding Gaussian noise to clean physiological signals at fixed physiological state (≥10 SNR levels). Measure ground truth SNR per segment. Apply conformal prediction with symmetric intervals. Bin segments by SNR (5 dB bins). Compute conditional coverage per bin. Fit linear regression: coverage ~ SNR_dB + physiological_state + skin_temp + feature_corruption. Test SNR coefficient. Perform Breusch-Pagan test on prediction errors. If SNR coefficient is non-significant after controlling for confounders (partial ρ < 0.2, p>0.05) and artificial noise addition at constant state shows no coverage trend across SNR bins, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage-SNR correlation not significant after controlling for physiological state, skin temperature, feature corruption (partial ρ < 0.2, p > 0.05), or artificial noise addition at constant state shows no coverage trend across SNR bins.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Segments with controlled SNR variation: induced by electrode gel degradation, motion, or simulated noise addition (≥10 SNR levels); ground truth SNR per segment (from clean reference or impedance measurements); conformal prediction with symmetric intervals (standard split conformal); prediction task with continuous target (HR, BP) or classification with score.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Low SNR segments coinciding with high-stress physiological states that inherently have higher prediction uncertainty, creating a spurious SNR-coverage correlation.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: The prediction model's errors are homoscedastic despite SNR variation (e.g., model is robust to noise), or the conformal interval width is large enough to cover the heteroscedastic errors, masking the effect.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Use a population dataset with clinical metadata: medication classes (beta-blockers, ACEi), comorbidities (HF, diabetes) (≥500 subjects). Segments labeled identically across subgroups (e.g., 'resting ECG'). Apply conformal prediction using only standard covariates (age, sex, BMI). Identify latent subgroups via clustering on signal features (GMM) or clinical metadata. Compute conditional coverage per subgroup. One-way ANOVA: coverage ~ subgroup. Post-hoc pairwise tests (Tukey) for beta-blocker users vs. non-users. Match subgroups on age, severity, SQI, segment type (propensity score matching). Paired t-test on matched pairs. If after matching, coverage does not differ across subgroups (ANOVA p>0.05, η²<0.05) and beta-blocker users vs. non-users show Δ<2% in matched strata, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: After matching on age, severity, signal quality, segment type distribution, coverage does not differ across subgroups (ANOVA p > 0.05, η² < 0.05), or beta-blocker users vs. non-users show Δ < 2% in matched strata.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Population dataset with clinical metadata: medication classes (beta-blockers, ACEi), comorbidities (HF, diabetes) (≥500 subjects); segments labeled identically across subgroups (e.g., 'resting ECG'); conformal prediction using only standard covariates (age, sex, BMI); post-hoc subgroup identification via clustering on signal features or clinical metadata.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Comorbidities and medications correlating with age and disease severity, which are the true drivers of coverage disparities, not the unmeasured heterogeneity per se.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient clinical metadata to identify relevant latent subgroups; or the conformal features used are insensitive to the physiological differences induced by medications/comorbidities (e.g., using only heart rate, not HRV).

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Sub-sample physiological recordings (ECG, EEG, accelerometer) into segments of varying lengths (10s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s). For each length, repeat random calibration/test splits (100x). Compute mean coverage and variance across splits. Fit power-law: log(variance) ~ log(segment_length). Test slope = -1 (t-test). Estimate effective_dof = segment_length / τ. Plot coverage variance vs. effective_dof across signal types. Determine minimum segment length for stability via bootstrap. If coverage variance does not decrease with segment length after matching effective degrees of freedom (partial correlation ρ > -0.2, p>0.05) or minimum stable segment length < 2*τ for high-autocorrelation signals, the hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage variance does not decrease with segment length after matching effective degrees of freedom (partial correlation ρ > -0.2, p > 0.05), or minimum stable segment length < 2*τ for high-autocorrelation signals.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Physiological signals with varying temporal correlation: ECG (high autocorr), EEG (lower), accelerometer (very low) (≥20 subjects, ≥10min each); segments of varying lengths: 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s; fixed calibration set size, varying only segment length; repeated random splits (≥100) to estimate coverage variance.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Feature extraction reliability decreasing with segment length (e.g., HRV metrics require minimum duration) causing coverage variance that is attributed to nonconformity score estimation but actually due to feature quality.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: The autocorrelation time constant τ is very short relative to the shortest segment tested, so effective degrees of freedom are already sufficient even at 10s, masking the segment-length effect.
